CLARITY ACT COMPROMISE BANS STABLECOIN REWARDS FROM LOOKING LIKE BANK INTEREST

Senators Thom Tillis
industry.description:
CLARITY ACT COMPROMISE BANS STABLECOIN REWARDS FROM LOOKING LIKE BANK INTEREST

Senators Thom Tillis (R-NC) and Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) have issued a joint statement confirming a bipartisan compromise on Section 404 of the CLARITY Act, signaling the deal is effectively locked in. 

The deal bars stablecoin rewards from mimicking bank deposit interest. That directly addresses the banking industry's core fear of deposit flight. 

Crypto firms can still offer other customer rewards. Journalist Eleanor Terrett (@EleanorTerrett) says the language signals the compromise is final. 

However, banking trade groups remain opposed. Both senators closed with a pointed line, saying they "respectfully agree to disagree."

P
industry.description:
Spent a week in Bangkok at Money20/20 Asia last month and almost nobody was talking about crypto.

Payment processors, banks, compliance teams, traditional finance operators. The conversations were about stablecoins settling cross-border payments, regulatory clarity, and implementation timelines.

No one cared about CT narratives. No one was asking about the latest L2 or speculate at what TVL megaeth will launch. They were working through the practical details of moving money more efficiently.

Institutions aren't coming into crypto because the tech is exciting. They're coming because it solves a real problem they've had forever - moving money across borders is slow and expensive, and stablecoins make it faster and cheaper.

That's it. That's the whole thesis.

Every meaningful wave of innovation in financial infrastructure comes down to two questions: can you do this faster, and can you do this cheaper? Crypto, specifically stablecoins on payment rails, answers yes to both.

CT argues about the tech while Institutions just want the cheaper wire transfer.
